relevance_note: The paper identifies homozygous splice-site mutations in the SSADH gene in four named patients: "patients OD, PD, and ZZ were homozygous for a GrT transversion at the first base of intron 9".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from hand-chosen values and spans, and a second script checked every span verbatim. Table 2 (enzyme activities) has subjects as rows under section headers 'Family of ZZ:' and 'Family of OD and PD:'; relatives labelled 'Father', 'Mother', 'Male sibling', 'Female sibling', 'Sibling (male)' were mapped to the relative labels by those section headers (spans quote the row only, because the header is not contiguous with the row). Relative labels follow the Figure 3 legend wording (Father/Mother/Brother/Sister of ZZ; Father/Mother/Brother of OD and PD; 'SM mother' -> 'mother of SM'). AC's parents have no stated individual sexes, so they are 'parent of AC' and 'parent of AC 2'. The gene is printed as 'SSADH gene'; the alleles are named 'ALDH4A1*1' (GrT, intron 9) and 'ALDH4A1*2' (GrA, intron 5) in the Introduction; gene_symbol_as_stated records 'SSADH'. No HGVS, transcript or genomic coordinates are printed (GenBank Y11192 is the deposited cDNA sequence, not stated as the variant reference). Inheritance for the homozygous patients is 'inherited unspecified parent' because both named parents are stated heterozygous carriers (the enum has no biallelic value); siblings' and parents' inheritance left 'not reported'. Group statements: 'The patients in the present study are moderately affected, exhibiting developmental and speech delays, hyporeflexia, and behavioral problems, including mild autism' was applied to OD, PD, ZZ and AC as inferred from group statement; 'mild autism' was NOT assigned to anyone because 'including' does not say which patients had it (autism checklist left not reported). 'At the initial presentation, all patients had increased GHB' applied to the four the same way. SM and IA are SSADH-deficient patients in whom neither mutation was found (wild-type-size amplicons; homozygous for presence of exon 9); they and SM's mother (Figure 3 lane 13) get individual rows but no variant rows. The 11 further patients in 10 families and 9 family members screened for the two mutations are described only as counts and get no rows; cohort_size_as_stated is null because no single study total is stated. Previously published persons: the 1981 first case (Jakobs et al. 1981; 'a child presenting with neurological abnormalities') and the Gibson et al. 1997 patient with mild oculomotor problems and truncal ataxia were included under the v4 passing-mention rule; the Gibson 1997 patient may conceivably be one of the four studied patients (whose clinical findings were also reported in Gibson et al. 1997), but the description (mild, near age-appropriate vocabulary) differs from the 'moderately affected' four, so kept separate. Not given rows: the 'Other patients' of DeVivo et al. 1988 (plural, no individual facts), the 'at least two patients' with seizures on vigabatrin (Gibson et al. 1989; Matern et al. 1996; not attributable person by person), the other adult case mentioned with ZZ, and the autopsied fetus (Chambliss et al. 1993; only absent enzyme activity, i.e. the diagnosis). Possible inconsistencies in the paper: (1) Figure 3 legend lane 8 reads 'Patient DP (sister of OD)' while the text names the siblings OD and PD; DP was taken to be PD and PD's sex recorded as female from this legend. (2) The text says SSADH activities from 'one of the families (three patients and their family members)' are in Table 2, but Table 2 splits them into 'Family of ZZ' and 'Family of OD and PD'; the text also calls ZZ a cousin of OD and PD 'from one family'. (3) 'Intermediate activities were observed in parents' and siblings' cell lines' versus the ZZ family members' activities described as 'very low' and 'considerably below ... the values expected in heterozygotes'; ZZ's relatives were recorded with 'very low SSADH activity'. Consanguinity was recorded only for the four patients (stated); not propagated to their siblings. No stacked cells in this paper.
